transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we discussed previously, the school's annual emergency evacuation exercise must be completed during the fall term, and I'm responsible for giving final approval to the exercise plan. The draft plan currently calls for a standard evacuation alarm, assembly in the east courtyard, and a general family notice. However, before I can approve it, school policy requires me to review the exercise plan with the nurse, counselor, facilities manager, and family liaison. I'd like to get that review process started today. Could each of you share your thoughts on the draft plan and any concerns or suggestions you might have?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a concern about the draft plan. A student's current seizure action plan requires a nurse or trained backup to accompany the student during any evacuation exercise and requires a designated medical-support station at the assembly area. I confirmed the plan with the student's family this week, but the exercise draft has not been updated to account for these requirements.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a concern as well. Two students have documented trauma accommodations requiring an announced walkthrough instead of a surprise alarm exercise, and a supervised opt-out location must be available for either student who cannot participate. I reviewed these accommodations this week, but they are not yet recorded in the exercise plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an important concern about the assembly area. The east courtyard is closed for resurfacing during the exercise window, so it can't be used. However, the fire marshal has approved the west field as a temporary assembly area. I received the closure and approval confirmation this week, but the facilities copy of the draft plan still lists the east courtyard, so it needs to be updated to reflect the west field instead.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a concern about the family notification portion of the draft plan. The district family-notification procedure requires at least 72 hours of advance notice for this exercise, and notices must be available in Spanish, Somali, and Vietnamese. I confirmed the language requirement with the district translation office this week, but the draft only says that a general notice will be sent — it doesn't specify the 72-hour advance notice or the required languages.
transcript.speaker: A5

Update the exercise plan to designate the west field as the assembly area, replacing the east courtyard which is closed for resurfacing during the exercise window.
Update the family notice to specify at least 72 hours of advance notice and ensure notices are available in English, Spanish, Somali, and Vietnamese.
Circulate the updated exercise plan to the nurse, counselor, facilities manager, and family liaison for confirmation before final approval.
